fact: The Plateforme de Dématérialisation des Recettes des Collectivités Locales (PDRCL) was designed, integrated and is managed by ACSI, an agency under the finance ministry, which presented it as a purely national development.

The finance ministry says PDRCL has a back-office module for local government agents and a market-collector module (Zando collecte) that enrols taxpayers, records revenues by payment mode and tracks each taxpayer's operations.
A final validation workshop for PDRCL was opened by the finance ministry on 12 February 2026 and ran to 14 February 2026, at Kintélé near Brazzaville.

The state's Agence congolaise des systèmes d'information (ACSI) was given responsibility for the local-revenue dematerialisation platform PDRCL by the 2025 finance law, and its director general presented it to the National Assembly's finance committee.

The local-revenue dematerialisation platform PDRCL passed final validation at a three-day workshop in Kintélé on 14 February 2026, which the finance ministry says now allows operational deployment; earlier workshops were held in the communes of Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire.

The finance ministry says PDRCL integrates local-collectivity revenues into one coherent information system, and workshop recommendations concern producing the notice of sums due and the receipt from liquidation statements sent by the originating directorates.
PDRCL was developed in-house by the state agency ACSI and organised under the finance ministry, which describes it as built against external dependence.
The platform was validated after workshops with the communes of Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire; no count of local governments live is given.

ACSI presented PDRCL to the Mayor of Brazzaville on 30 April 2026 as recording every transaction in real time through field agents' mobile terminals, with a dashboard for the municipal authority; no register of payers is stated.
ACSI made the official presentation of PDRCL to the Mayor of Brazzaville on 30 April 2026, after the February validation.

A pilot of the PDRCL was to be deployed at the Ndjindji central market in Pointe-Noire, after municipal staff were trained; one municipality, no count of others. The article carries no date, so the published month is used.
The PDRCL is described as managing vendors' taxes, with a census of traders in an official database and a field tool for controllers (Zando Collecte); at the pilot stage.
The PDRCL was developed by ACSI, the state information-systems agency, with the municipality of Pointe-Noire.
Municipal staff of Pointe-Noire were trained on the PDRCL and a pilot at Ndjindji market was to follow; dated by the publication month, not by the body.
On 24 February 2026 the digital-transformation steering unit met at the Ministry of Finance, Budget and Public Portfolio with ACSI and the PDRCL project team, which ACSI runs.
The PDRCL was demonstrated in detail on 24 February 2026 and ACSI was said to be preparing its imminent deployment; nothing is stated as live.
ACSI's general procurement notice of 4 September 2025 lists, from its 2025 investment budget, IT equipment for developing and implementing the PDRCL on behalf of the Ministry of the Interior.
The notice places the PDRCL with the Ministry of the Interior as client and ACSI as buyer.
